item.title: Some families flee Kansas as gender-affirming care ban for minors takes effect
item.description: In January, all access to hormone treatments and other gender-affirming care for transgender youth will end in Kansas. Some families have already moved to avoid the ban. Continue reading ...

item.title: Kansas governor doubtful GOP legislators can pull off congressional redistricting
item.description: Gov. Laura Kelly predicted Tuesday the 2026 Legislature wouldn’t muster enough political support to implement a new congressional district map splitting Johnson County and making it easier to defeat U.S. Rep. Sharice Davids in the midterm election. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence Humane Pet of the Week: Unflappable brindle shepherd mix Cardi B. is not the drama
item.description: Unlike her namesake, 3-year-old brindle shepherd mix Cardi B. doesn't have to ask if she's the drama. She's guaranteed to be a human's peace. Continue reading ...

item.title: New edition of first volume of ‘Embattled Lawrence’ released
item.description: An updated version of "Embattled Lawrence Vol. 1," an original work detailing history of Lawrence, aims to fill in more gaps than its predecessor. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence City Commission votes to keep Community Building open for exercise access on trial basis
item.description: Lawrence city commissioners on Tuesday voted to keep the Community Building open and free to residents for a three-month trial basis once access fees to use the city's other recreation centers go into effect in January. Continue reading ...

item.title: Lawrence City Commission general public comment for Dec. 16, 2025
item.description: Here’s the general public comment for the Lawrence City Commission’s Tuesday meeting, as public comment is no longer being broadcast. Continue reading ...

item.title: Kansas lawmakers may censor how universities talk about race in classes
item.description: A state law requires Kansas agencies and universities to eliminate any policies related to diversity, equity and inclusion. Republican lawmakers are questioning whether they should also regulate the content in college courses. Continue reading ...

item.title: Topeka man sentenced to nearly 52 years in murder of Lawrence musician
item.description: A Topeka man was sentenced Wednesday to nearly 52 years for the murder of a Lawrence musician, and the victim's family members said they were grateful for a sense of justice. Continue reading ...

item.title: Planning Commission recommends zoning changes for former Dragon’s Hoard site, Bert Nash housing
item.description: Planning commissioners gave nods of approval to one zoning request to allow houses to be built at the former Dragon's Hoard location and another for Bert Nash to construct apartments off Sixth and Rockledge. Continue reading ...

item.title: ‘We’re regressing’: Douglas County commissioners again bump tenant right to counsel program to back burner
item.description: Although Douglas County has expressed commitment to tenant right to counsel and has engaged in implementation discussions for months, a majority of county commissioners Wednesday opted instead to have county staff do more research on mediation. Continue reading ...
